chunks: What ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

If you did not know until the eclipse had passed, then came to know after that, then there is no salat of the eclipse upon you. But if one person informed you while you were asleep, and you came to know, then your eye overpowered you and you did not pray, then its qaḍāʾ is upon you. For the correct approach regarding this narration is that we interpret it to mean that when part of the disc was obscured and one was informed of that but did not pray, then qaḍāʾ was upon him; but if he did not know at all, then qaḍāʾ was not binding upon him. As for when the entire disc was obscured, then qaḍāʾ was upon him in every case, whether he knew or did not know; and if he had known, then ghusl was also upon him together with the qaḍāʾ, according to what we have explained previously.

key_terms.احْتَرَقَ: became obscured or eclipsed, referring here to the sun's disc
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in this ruling under specified conditions
key_terms.الْقُرْصِ: the solar disc referred to in describing partial or total eclipse
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: the eclipse for which the prescribed prayer is performed
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْكُسُوفِ: the ritual prayer legislated for an eclipse
key_terms.قَضَاؤُهَا: making up the missed eclipse prayer after its time has passed

ai.seo_question: When is qaḍāʾ of salat al-kusuf required if someone missed the eclipse prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling for missing salat al-kusuf and distinguishes between partial and total eclipse. It explains when qaḍāʾ becomes obligatory, depending on whether the person knew of the eclipse, and notes that in the case of a total eclipse with prior knowledge, ghusl is also required.
